fix: add automated tagging for private packages (#25)

The workflow wasn't creating git tags or GitHub releases because
`pnpm changeset tag` only works for packages published to npm.

Since this package has `"private": true` (GitHub releases only, no npm
publishing), changesets won't automatically create tags. This is by design -
changesets only tags packages that are actually published to npm.

This commit adds a new workflow step that runs after the Version Packages PR
is merged (when hasChangesets == false):
1. Reads version from package.json
2. Creates git tag (e.g., v2.0.2)
3. Pushes tag to GitHub
4. Creates GitHub Release from tag

This enables fully automated releases for non-npm packages.

Note: v2.0.1 was manually tagged and released to bootstrap this fix.
Future releases (v2.0.2+) will be fully automated.

fix: verify the first-party pin before mutating installed skills (#242)

The installer pins first-party skills to the current checkout's exact HEAD.
An unpushed HEAD cannot be fetched back from GitHub, but the failure landed
only after backup_selected_skills had already moved every selected skill
aside -- so a mistake that changes nothing semantically stranded the user's
entire skills directory and reported only "upload-pack: not our ref".

validated or anything is backed up, and memoise the fetch so the later install
reuses it instead of pulling the same commit twice. On failure, abort with
nothing changed and name the cause -- an unpushed commit -- alongside the three
ways out: push it, pass a pushed commit, or pass a released tag.

fix: let the installer run from anywhere (#244)

--version defaulted to the checkout's exact HEAD unconditionally, so the
script only worked from a checkout that happened to be pushed. An unpushed
commit aborted the install with "upload-pack: not our ref", and a stray copy
or a curl pipe refused outright -- despite this being the install path for
anyone who does not already have the repository.

Work the default out instead of assuming it, still pinning to an exact
immutable revision in every case: an explicit --version wins; otherwise HEAD
when that commit is actually on the remote, so a contributor installs what
they inspected; otherwise the latest release tag, read straight from the
remote so no local clone is needed. Falling back announces itself and names
both commits rather than changing the pin silently.

Also drops the "$0" interpolation from the preflight error, which printed
"bash --version ..." when the script was piped, and rewords it to fit both
causes rather than blaming --version.

fix: never take the version from an unrelated repository (#245)

A piped install leaves BASH_SOURCE unset, so `dirname ""` resolved to `.` --
the directory the user happened to be standing in. Running the one-liner from
inside any other git repository therefore pinned this installer to *that*
repository's HEAD, and the install died on `upload-pack: not our ref` for a
commit that was never in this project. The earlier fallback did not help: its
reachability probe consulted the same foreign checkout's origin/main, which
happily confirmed the foreign commit.

The script's location now counts only when it is a real file inside a real
checkout of this repository, verified through its remotes. Anything else --
a piped install, a stray copy, someone else's repo -- resolves the latest
release from the remote instead. Reachability likewise never trusts a foreign
checkout. `--version <tag>` now resolves against the remote too, so it works
with no checkout at all.

Test stubs gain a published tag because release resolution is now reachable
from paths that previously stopped at a checkout HEAD, and two comments avoid
the literal bootstrap pattern the docs guard rejects.
